cards.front: What is the definition of the generalized (conjugate) momentum $p_j$?
How is the generalized force $Q_j$ defined via virtual work?
cards.back: $\delta W = \sum_j Q_j \delta q_j$, so $Q_j$ is the coefficient of $\delta q_j$ in the virtual work of all applied forces.

cards.front: Write Lagrange's equations when non-conservative generalized forces $Q_j$ are present.
If every force derives from a potential $V(q)$, what is the expression for $Q_j$?
cards.back: $Q_j=-\frac{\partial V}{\partial q_j}$ (so the $Q_j$ term can be absorbed into $L=T-V$).

cards.front: Express the generalized force in terms of the Cartesian forces $\mathbf{F}_i$.
Under what conditions is the generalized momentum $p_j$ a constant of the motion?
cards.back: When $q_j$ is cyclic ($\partial L/\partial q_j=0$) and the corresponding generalized force vanishes ($Q_j=0$). Then Lagrange's equation reduces to $\dot{p}_j=0$.

cards.front: For a velocity-independent potential, relate $p_j$ to the kinetic energy $T$.
cards.back: $p_j=\frac{\partial T}{\partial\dot{q}_j}$ because $V$ does not depend on $\dot{q}_j$.

cards.front: Derive the time derivative of $p_j$ directly from the definition and Lagrange's equation.
cards.back: From $p_j=\partial L/\partial\dot{q}_j$ and Lagrange, $\dot{p}_j=\partial L/\partial q_j+Q_j$.
